---
title: "Are we sure the model is correctly using the NACA 0006 airfoil?"
---


The section is checked three ways — that the geometry is what it claims, that
every surface carries it, and that NeuralFoil returns a symmetric polar from it
— and then the choice itself is tested by giving each surface the section its
own chords imply.

::: {#c92430cb .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
af = asb.Airfoil("naca0006")
print(f"max thickness {af.max_thickness():.4f}, max camber {af.max_camber():.6f}")
for w in mceagle.wings:
    print(f"{w.name:11s} sections carry {set(x.airfoil.name for x in w.xsecs)}")

a2 = np.linspace(-4, 4, 9)
for Re in [1.6e3, 3.6e4]:                 # the fin tip, and the mean chord
    r = af.get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a2, Re=Re)
    print(f"Re {Re:7.0f}: CL(0) {np.array(r['CL'])[4]:+.2e}, "
          f"dCL/dalpha {np.polyfit(a2, np.array(r['CL']), 1)[0]:.4f} /deg "
          f"(thin-airfoil 0.1097), confidence "
          f"{float(np.array(r['analysis_confidence'])[0]):.2f}")
```

``` {.python .cell-code}
def swap(af_w, af_h, af_v):
    """The airframe rebuilt with a chosen section on each surface."""
    xs = lambda le, eta, c, af, **kw: asb.WingXSec(xyz_le=le, chord=c,
                                                   airfoil=af, **kw)
    return asb.Airplane(
        name="v", fuselages=mceagle.fuselages, s_ref=S_w, c_ref=c_w, b_ref=b_w,
        xyz_ref=[x_qc_w, 0, 0],
        wings=[
            asb.Wing(name="Wing", symmetric=True, xsecs=[
                xs([x_le_w, e*b_w/2, e*z_tip], e, c, af_w)
                for e, c in zip(wing_eta, wing_c)]),
            asb.Wing(name="Stabilizer", symmetric=True, xsecs=[
                xs([x_le_h, e*b_h/2, z_h], e, c, af_h, twist=i_h)
                for e, c in zip(stab_eta, stab_c)]),
            asb.Wing(name="Fin", xsecs=[
                xs([x_te_v - c, 0, e*b_v], e, c, af_v)
                for e, c in zip(fin_eta, fin_c)]),
        ])


ALPHA = np.linspace(-15, 15, 121)
BAND = (ALPHA >= 0) & (ALPHA <= 8)
mp0 = mass_properties()

for label, ap in [("all 0006, as modelled", mceagle),
                  ("stab 0008, fin 0013", swap(*map(asb.Airfoil,
                       ["naca0006", "naca0008", "naca0013"])))]:
    p = polars(ALPHA, V=6.0, airplane=ap)
    CL, Cm = np.array(p["CL"]), np.array(p["Cm"])
    x_np = x_qc_w - np.polyfit(CL[BAND], Cm[BAND], 1)[0] * c_w
    x_cg = x_np - 0.10 * c_w
    b = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane=ap, op_point=asb.OperatingPoint(
        velocity=6.0, alpha=4.0, beta=np.array([-2.0, 2.0]))).run()
    Cn = np.array(b["Cn"])
    print(f"{label:22s} x_np {x_np*1e3:6.1f} mm, ballast "
          f"{mp0.mass*(mp0.x_cg - x_cg)/x_cg*1e3:5.2f} g, Cn_beta "
          f"{(Cn[1]-Cn[0])/4/np.pi*180:+.4f} /rad")

```

```
stab 0008, fin 0013    x_np  150.1 mm, ballast  3.82 g, Cn_beta -0.0085 /rad
```

:::


**Answer.** Yes, mechanically. The geometry is a true NACA 0006 — 6.00% thick,
zero camber — every section of all three surfaces carries it, and NeuralFoil
returns CL(0) = 0 to machine precision with a slope near thin-airfoil theory,
still at 0.94 confidence down at the fin tip's Re of 1,600.

What is not right is the reason recorded for choosing it. Six percent matches
the wing's mean chord and nothing else: the same 5 mm foam is 7.9% of the
stabilizer's chord and 12.8% of the fin's. Matching those makes the model
worse. NeuralFoil's smooth sections shed lift-curve slope quickly at this scale
— at the fin's Re of 15,600 it runs 0.081, 0.066, 0.048, 0.018 per degree
across 6, 8, 10 and 13% thick — so a 13% fin flips Cn_beta from +0.0957 to
−0.0085 and the aircraft loses directional stability. A square-cut plate does
not behave that way, because its sharp edge fixes separation and reattachment.
One thin section on every surface is therefore the right model of a flat plate,
and being thinner than the tail's true t/c is the point rather than an error.

One consequence for later work: the Cn_beta above is taken about the model's
moment reference at the wing quarter-chord. About the ballasted CG it is
+0.0485 /rad, a little over half as much, because the fin's arm is shorter from
there.
